$comment: V-80 and A15. Transferred kilobytes for a cold load at 390x844, per route, and the landing's height. EVERY PUBLIC BUDGET HERE WAS RE-RECORDED ON 6 OCTOBER 2026 AGAINST A REBUILT INSTRUMENT, AND EVERY ONE OF THEM CAME DOWN. The previous entry said the real fix was the instrument and not these numbers. It was right, and this is that fix landing. WHAT THE OLD 79 KB OF VARIANCE ACTUALLY WAS. The old note guessed that `waitUntil: 'networkidle'` was settling at different points while lazy assets arrived. The blame was right and the mechanism was wrong, and the mechanism is what made a fix possible. Ten loads of /welcome, logging bytes per URL, gave nine readings between 660 and 673 and one of 730. The outlier had fetched two chunks the other nine never fetched at all: 64 KB holding the Supabase browser client and 8 KB holding the sign-up terms control. Neither belongs to /welcome. Both belong to /sign-in and /sign-up, and they arrived because NEXT PREFETCHES THE ROUTES A PAGE LINKS TO. Tagging requests by header confirmed it everywhere: /check issues twelve router fetches for /, /start, /search, /about and /r; /sign-in issues sixteen for /terms, /privacy, /eula, /forgot-password and /sign-in/code. Not one tagged request was the page's own data. So the extra bytes were never late, they were CONDITIONAL, and waiting longer would not have helped: a further seven seconds of quiet after networkidle added nothing on any of the nine clean runs. Whether the router gets a link's prefetch away before the measurement ends depends on viewport intersection and idle scheduling, which is a coin toss. That is why widening these budgets could never converge. THE NEW INSTRUMENT, IN THREE PARTS (`scripts/check-weight.mjs`, which carries the full reasoning). Router prefetches are aborted and therefore not counted, so a route is charged for its own bytes and nothing else. `networkidle` is replaced by `load` plus an explicit settle: nothing in flight and 1,500 ms of silence, capped at 15 s so a polling page cannot hang the gate. Each route is measured twice in fresh contexts and the HIGHER reading is the verdict. The gate prints the spread and the dropped-prefetch count on every line, so the instrument reports on itself. NOT COUNTING A PREFETCH IS AN ACCOUNTING JUDGEMENT AND IS STATED AS ONE. A prefetch of /search is /search's weight, it already has its own line in this file, and charging it to /check as well both double-counted it and made /check's budget move when a page it merely links to changed. Every tagged request was checked to be a neighbouring route and not the page's own content before any of them was blocked. What this gate no longer answers is how many bytes a visitor pulls in total while the next tap is warmed. That is a fair question and it is not a per-route ratchet. THE EVIDENCE, FIVE PASSES EACH ON ONE PRODUCTION BUILD. Spread per route BEFORE, in KB: / 9, /welcome 70, /sign-in 21, /sign-up/email 21, /check 12, /move-in-cost 13, /for-agents 22, /guides/avoiding-rental-scams 6. AFTER: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0. The five full runs of the new gate (ten readings per route) returned the SAME integer every time on all eight routes. THE NUMBERS, AND THE RULE UNCHANGED: measured max plus the larger of 20 KB and the route's observed spread, rounded up to 5 KB. Measured max then budget: / 496 and 520; /welcome 644 and 665; /sign-in 615 and 635; /sign-up/email 617 and 640; /check 434 and 455; /move-in-cost 448 and 470; /for-agents 452 and 475; /guides/avoiding-rental-scams 438 and 460. The spread is zero, so the 20 KB floor is what every margin is. /for-agents went from 640 to 475 and /check from 630 to 455: the first is the variance going away, the second is mostly /search's and /about's chunks no longer being billed to /check. A 70 KB regression on /for-agents, which a 640 budget would have let through without a word, now fails the gate three times over. READ ON A CONTAINER, NOT IN CI, AND THAT IS THE ONE SOFT SPOT. The readings above come from a local production build with no NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and no NEXT_PUBLIC_MAPTILER_KEY, while CI's front-door job builds with both. Before this change the two agreed inside a few KB on every route (CI / read 505 to 510 against 500 to 509 locally, CI /check 590 to 599 against 594 to 606), so 20 KB of margin should hold. The first CI run after this commit is the one to look at: if a route reads OVER by a handful of KB, that is the environment gap and not a regression, and the honest repair is to record that route from CI's own reading rather than to widen the rule. Ratchet down, never up without a reason in the commit. THE SEVEN SIGNED-IN ROUTES ARE STILL NULL, AND THAT IS HONEST RATHER THAN UNFINISHED: CI skips them for want of a WEIGHT_COOKIE, and the only cookie obtainable without credentials comes from `tests/gate-stub-session.mjs`, whose stub serves nothing, so the pages render empty and not-found states and their weight is not the weight of the page. They can be budgeted the first time CI mints a WEIGHT_COOKIE from real QA credentials, and not before (ci.yml names the two secrets that unlock it). /wallet was retired on 25 September and is gone from the list. A null budget is reported and never fails. Heights are a ratchet too: the UIUX item 9 targets are under 8,000px at 390 and under 6,500px at 1440, and the landing is above both. The front-door re-audit of 30 September measured 9,728 and 8,658; this check now reads 9,455 and 8,627, so the ceiling holds that height and must only come down. RAISED ON 7 OCTOBER 2026, WITH THE REASON (the founder's restoration). The founder asked for Vallo's real glossy logo in the startup and the original 3D art on Get Started and the landing hero, in place of a flat vector redraw and the matte set. That art is the weight: the startup's two real-logo images (about 38 KB, on every route, since the overlay renders before the gate can know the visit) and the 3D scene and objects. CI read / 573, /welcome 731 and /move-in-cost 477 on the restoring commit; each budget is that reading plus the same 20 KB margin, rounded up to 5: / 595, /welcome 755, /move-in-cost 500. Recompressing the logo images saved about 3 KB at visible cost, so they stay as they are. RAISED ONCE, AT 390 ONLY, ON 7 OCTOBER 2026, WITH THE REASON: the founder asked for the two rooms that carried his 3D art back on the landing (the bento and the AI room, deleted on 6 October), after reading the page as unchanged. With them the page reads 10,041px at 390 (local production build, empty catalogue) and 8,009px at 1440, which is still under its 8,700 ceiling. On a phone the bento is a swipe row (one card tall) and the AI room's conversation panel is 26rem, or 19rem when there are no listing cards to show, so the rooms cost what they must and no more. The 390 ceiling moves from 9,800 to 10,400: the measured height plus the conversation panel's cards when the catalogue has listings (112px) and a margin for CI's catalogue. The target is unchanged, and the ratchet runs down from here. LOWERED ON 17 OCTOBER 2026, WITH THE REASON, AND ONE ROUTE ADDED. The welcome screen's interest cards imported their constants from lib/interests/schema, which builds zod at import time, so /welcome carried zod in its first load (85 KB gzipped). They now import lib/interests/model. Same instrument, local production build: /welcome read 702 before and 615 after, five readings, spread 0. CI read /welcome 29 KB above the local build on the restoring commit (731 against 702), so the new budget is the local reading plus that gap plus the 20 KB margin, rounded up to 5: 755 to 665. The documentation was unguarded and regressed by 640 KB without a word: the chapter rail, a client component, imported the chapter module and with it every chapter, the whole i18n dictionary and zod (/docs/quick-start read 1,047 KB; 411 after the fix). /docs/quick-start joins the list at 411 plus 20, rounded up to 5: 435. Like /for-agents it is a plain public page, where CI and local agreed within a few KB; if the first CI run reads it over by a handful, record it from CI's reading, as the note above says, rather than widening the rule.
